title: Cells
summary: A fixture pack with one item of every kind, verified and not.

concepts.name: Cell
concepts.summary: The smallest unit of life that can live on its own.

explain.text: A cell is the smallest living thing that can survive on its own. Every plant, animal and fungus is made of them, and many living things are a single cell. A thin membrane wraps each one and decides what comes in and goes out. Inside, many cells keep their DNA in a nucleus, which acts as the cell's library of instructions for making proteins.

concepts.name: Organelle
concepts.summary: A part inside a cell that does one job, the way an organ does in a body.

items.prompt: What does the cell membrane do?
choices: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
Makes most of the cell's ATP
items.explanation: The membrane is a barrier that lets some things through and keeps others out.

items.prompt: What does the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell hold?
items.explanation: The nucleus holds the chromosomes, which are made of DNA.

items.prompt: Put the steps of making a protein for export in order.
steps: DNA is transcribed in the nucleus
The Golgi apparatus packages the protein
items.explanation: Transcription, then export of the message, then translation, then packaging.

items.prompt: Tap the part that holds the cell's DNA.
items.explanation: The large round body in the middle is the nucleus.

items.prompt: Which organelle makes most of an animal cell's ATP?
items.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration, which makes most of the ATP.

items.prompt: Which organelle packages proteins for export from the cell?
items.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies proteins and sends them on in vesicles.

items.prompt: Put these in order from smallest to largest.
items.explanation: Atoms make molecules, molecules make organelles, organelles sit in cells, and cells make tissues.

items.prompt: Tap the organelle that makes most of the cell's ATP.
items.explanation: The red bean-shaped body is a mitochondrion.

items.prompt: Which of these is a cell?
items.explanation: A bacterium is a cell; a virus is not.

verification.note: Too easy to guess from the wording.
